claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 normally requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve adequate densification.
Single-phase ZrB2 suffers from oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion during service.
Approximately 3 wt% Si can be incorporated substitutionally into ZrB2 during sintering.
Si addition promotes densification of ZrB2 at 1700–1800 °C.
Si substitution alters ZrB2 grain-boundary chemistry and produces a Si-rich intergranular phase.
The Si-rich intergranular phase converts during oxidation into a protective SiO2 or borosilicate layer.
The protective SiO2-related layer impedes further oxidation and liquid-metal ingress.
Si facilitates lower-temperature densification through enhanced diffusion and liquid-phase-sintering effects.
Si-doped ZrB2 will achieve full densification when sintered at approximately 1700–1800 °C.
Low-temperature Si-doped ZrB2 will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to or greater than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 will show lower oxidation weight gain than both traditional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will show lower liquid plating-metal corrosion rates than both traditional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Approximately 3 wt% Si is within the solubility limit relevant to the proposed ZrB2 process.
Increasing Si beyond the proposed low level may cause phase separation or unwanted silicide formation.
The beneficial oxidation and corrosion effects will remain effective at service temperatures up to approximately 1800 °C.
The intervention will be effective in liquid plating baths representative of the intended corrosive service conditions.
